entries.trigger: Detention of the voluntary inpatient so the assessment can be conducted
entries.quote: The voluntary inpatient can be detained under the order at the authorised hospital for up to 6 hours from the time when the order was made to enable the assessment to be conducted
entries.anchor: The time the Form 2 order was made

entries.trigger: Detention so the referred person can be taken to the authorised hospital or other place
entries.quote: may make an order authorising the person’s detention for up to 24 hours from the time when the order is made
entries.anchor: The time the Form 3A order was made

caveat.quote: The person cannot continue to be detained if the referral expires before the person is taken to the authorised hospital or other place

entries.trigger: Longest continuous detention under section 28 orders, when the referral was made in a metropolitan area
entries.quote: The person cannot be detained under orders made under this section for a continuous period of more than — (a)if the place where the referral is made is in a metropolitan area — 72 hours
entries.anchor: The time the first section 28 detention order (this Form 3A) was made

caveat.quote: The person cannot continue to be detained if the referral expires before the person is taken to the authorised hospital or other place

entries.trigger: Longest continuous detention under section 28 orders, when the referral was made outside a metropolitan area
entries.leadIn: The person cannot be detained under orders made under this section for a continuous period of more than —
entries.quote: (b)if the place where the referral is made is outside a metropolitan area — 144 hours
entries.anchor: The time the first section 28 detention order (this Form 3A) was made

caveat.quote: The person cannot continue to be detained if the referral expires before the person is taken to the authorised hospital or other place

entries.trigger: Detention to take the person to the hospital, if a section 62 order is made
entries.condition: Only if an order under section 62(1) is made to detain the person so they can be taken to the hospital
entries.quote: may make an order authorising the continuation of the person’s detention for up to 24 hours from the time when the order under section 61(1)(a) or (c) is made
entries.anchor: The time this order under section 61(1)(a) or (c) was made

entries.trigger: Longest continuous detention, if a section 62 order is made
entries.condition: Only if an order under section 62(1) is made to detain the person so they can be taken to the hospital
entries.quote: A person cannot be detained under orders made under this section for a continuous period of more than 72 hours
entries.anchor: The time this order under section 61(1)(a) or (c) was made

entries.trigger: Confirmation of the community treatment order, if it was made under section 75
entries.condition: Only if this community treatment order was made under section 75. Form 5A is also used for orders made under other sections
entries.quote: Within 72 hours after the time when the community treatment order is made, it must be confirmed by
entries.anchor: The time the community treatment order was made

entries.trigger: Advising the Chief Mental Health Advocate that a restriction on freedom of communication has been made
entries.quote: must, within 24 hours after the time when the order is made, advise the Chief Mental Health Advocate that the order has been made
entries.anchor: The time the order was made

entries.trigger: First review of the restriction on freedom of communication (the Act requires a review before the end of each 24-hour period the order is in force)
entries.quote: A psychiatrist must, before the end of each 24-hour period that an order made under subsection (1) is in force, review the order and confirm, amend or revoke it
entries.anchor: The time the order was made
